description: Gentle-AI configures the AI coding agents you already use: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, and more. Choose persistent memory, Organic-Driven Development, curated skills, MCP servers, personas, and optional bounded review. Open source, no agent lock-in.

latest_release.name: v4.4.0 — Antigravity 1.4 Parity, Faster Gentle Shell Launches and Safer Windows Restores
latest_release.body:
Gentle AI v4.4.0 is a minor release over v4.3.1. Restores and rollbacks now work when Windows redirects `%APPDATA%` outside the profile, and a workspace uninstall snapshot can be restored on its own. JSON and JSONC configs that start with a UTF-8 BOM keep the user's keys instead of being merged into an empty object. The Windows Full Suite is green again and now runs on every pull request. Antigravity (agy 1.4) reaches parity with native Judgment Day agents, per-role model tiers and guidance that fits agy's 24 KB rule budget. Gentle Shell provisions Stable from a reviewed gentle-pi supplier list, launches in a fraction of the time, and publishes `gs` on Windows. Codex honors `CODEX_HOME` end to end. The provider contract stays byte-frozen at `1.4.0`.

## Provenance

- **Previous stable:** `v4.3.1` → `2dba7784114fff57864519c4c0d067e952a8c98b`
- **Release target:** `v4.4.0` → `55240afb100ad6d2ef5fbe16f7be33a7693f77ad`
- **Release workflow:** [run 42396346091](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/actions/runs/42396346091)
- **Verification:** preflight, release, and verify jobs all succeeded.
- **Provider contract:** `1.4.0`

## What's new

### Antigravity 1.4 parity

Antigravity now receives the Judgment Day native agents (`jd-judge-a`, `jd-judge-b`, `jd-fix-agent`) that Claude Code, Cursor and Kiro already had. Their model tier (`inherit`, `flash_lite`, `flash`, `pro`) can be picked per role in the installer and changed later from Configure Models. Gentle AI guidance is rendered as owned agy rule files that each stay under agy's 24 KB limit, and legacy Gentle AI sections in `GEMINI.md` are migrated into them.

Included work: [#5931](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5931), [#5938](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5938), [#5939](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5939), [#5940](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5940), [#5941](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5941), [#5942](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5942) (issue #5930).

### Gentle Shell Stable follows a reviewed gentle-pi supplier list

Gentle Shell now ships a reviewed list of gentle-pi releases, each pinned by its npm tarball SRI and installer hash, and reads it live with a fail-safe fallback. Stable installs provision the newest reviewed release, the Windows provisioner reads the same list, installs without a list authenticate supplier files at launch, and the Stable update check detects an outdated gentle-pi by its installed version and targets the newest listed release. gentle-pi 4.5.1 is the first reviewed entry.

Included work: [#5849](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5849), [#5852](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5852), [#5853](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5853), [#5863](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5863), [#5871](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5871), [#5873](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5873), [#5876](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5876) (issue #5845) by @decode2.

### Faster Gentle Shell launches

Standalone `gentle-shell`/`gs` launches spent 13 to 19 seconds re-verifying unchanged bytes on every start. Pinned binaries, the retained Main source and the installed graph are now checked against ctime-bound stamp caches and receipts that a prior full audit produced, so every check stays as strict while unchanged bytes are no longer re-read. Main launches drop to about 3.3 seconds and Stable launches from 2.81 to 0.33 seconds; a timing probe on the Windows runtime lane measured the Windows launch boundary at about 52 ms warm.

Included work: [#5920](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5920) (issue #5917), [#5960](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/pull/5960), [#5922](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle

detail.readme:
Gentle-AI™

The deterministic engineering environment for the AI agent you already use.

Website • Quickstart • Docs • Wiki


Your agent writes code, then forgets everything. It has no opinion about your project, and no way to prove what it did beyond asking you to read every line. Gentle-AI gives it memory, a workflow, and evidence.

See it in action

One prompt, from idea to reviewed commit: memory, workflow, and evidence in a real session.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa5c0cfe-06e7-4c0d-bd6e-8ac7cb934339

Prefer Spanish subtitles?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d2bc422-a4dd-4ecf-a04b-fcd3bea7fea9


If Gentle-AI made your agent worth trusting, a star helps other people find it.
WORKS WITH THE AGENT YOU ALREADY HAVE Pi · OpenCode · Claude Code · Codex · Cursor · VS Code Copilot · Gemini CLI · Kilo Code
Kimi Code · Kiro IDE · Qwen Code · Hermes · Antigravity · Windsurf · OpenClaw · Trae · Conductor 17 integrations · native configuration · compare capabilities →
## Support the project

We deliberately don't depend on investors: no outside agenda deciding the roadmap and no features locked behind paywalls.
Donations through GitHub Sponsors go straight into maintenance, new features and keeping everything free and ours.

Can't donate? A ⭐, a bug report or a pull request helps too.

Sponsorship never buys rankings, default selections or endorsements; see TRADEMARKS.md.
## Features --- ### Engram™ — Keep your project context The cost of a fresh session is not the tokens — it is you, re-explaining the same decisions every morning. Engram removes that: your agent writes down what it learns as it goes and reaches for it before it reaches for you, so context accumulates instead of resetting. **[Docs →](docs/engram.md)** --- ### ODD — Keep small work small Small changes should not need a planning pipeline, and larger work should not lose its context between sessions. **Organic Driven Development (ODD)** keeps understood changes lightweight and gives substantial, authorized work one recoverable feature document. Questions, reviews and proposals stay read-only until you ask for a change. The agent explores before changing code, checks the results, and keeps progress current so work can resume without rebuilding the plan. Tasks are sized by understanding, risk, and resumability, never by file count. A small task — understood, with contained risk, and resumable from the diff alone — runs inline: no subagents, no task document. Work becomes large only when it can't be resumed from the diff — several sessions, external waits, or requirements too long to survive compaction — never because of its size. The feature document of a large task holds your spec verbatim, and every handoff points at it instead of paraphrasing it. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/857a2195-34b8-4720-87af-f71bca3dec92 **[Docs →](docs/usage.md#organic-driven-development-odd)** --- ### Delegate for a reason — Not for size A subagent costs a fresh session, uncached reads, and a handoff. So the orchestrator delegates only when it can name the reason: | Reason | When it applies | | :--- | :--- | | **Exploration** | Understanding needs more than one inline batch (about 3 calls and 10k tokens) or more than about five sequential lookups; one read-only explorer returns a short map with `path:line` evidence | | **Parallel writers** | Two or more independent units of behavior (code, tests, and docs together) with disjoint edit surfaces, each needing several minutes of work: several files or roughly 100+ changed lines, because a subagent spends one to two minutes reading before it writes. A delivery that depends on another is not independent | | **Context backstop** | A long session hands its next bounded unit to a fresh worker | | **Independent verifier** | A change that names a high-risk item (data, security, shared contracts, concurrency, delivery, or no test that would catch a regression); never a native risk tier alone, an unclear or failed assessment, or the model that wrote the change | A trigger holds only when its condition truly holds; none holds by default, and when in doubt the parent works inline. Without a reason the parent writes inline, following its feature document. File count, task size, or a model price ratio never decide the route on their own. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccd96c9e-e0fd-4504-ad94-0302398f13a9 **[Docs →](docs/trigger-rules.md)** --- ### Measured — What proportional routing changed The routing rules above came from benchmarks, not intuition. These are Gentle Shell runs on a local benchmark with hidden acceptance suites; each cell is a single run (n=1), and cost is API-equivalent. | Scenario | Before | After | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 3-line bug in one function | 335 s · 56 turns · $0.339 | **77 s · 10 turns · $0.105** — inline, no subagents | | Bug rooted in shared logic | 479 s · $0.361 | **276 s · $0.207** — one explorer | | Data migration (high risk) | 559 s · $0.403 · needed a feedback round | 539 s · $0.555 · **accepted on the first round** — one independent verifier | | 73-line spec, 26 hidden checks | Paraphrased handoffs: 13 failing, still 23/26 after two feedback rounds | Spec passed by reference ([gentle-shell#1718](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/pull/1718)) | Against the same model in Codex CLI, with blind review of every solution, Gentle Shell was accepted on the first round in every cell and ranked higher on the medium (3 of 3 runs) and large tasks; it was close on the small one. The large task still took about three times longer (17.5–17.9 min vs 6.1 min) — that gap is open work. Sources: [gentle-shell#1723](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/pull/1723), [#1794](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/pull/1794), [#1713](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell/issues/1713). --- ### Test-first by default — Prove each requested rule ODD applies test-first development by default when a relevant runnable test and a clear expected outcome exist: capture a failing behavior test before implementation, make it pass, then refactor while tests stay green. Each requested rule gets one RED test, each touched existing command or option gets one test proving its previous behavior still holds, and nothing else is padded in. Without a meaningful runnable test, the agent explains the exception and runs applicable functional checks anyway. **[Docs →](docs/usage.md#organic-driven-development-odd)** --- ### RDD — Check finished work at the right depth Receipt-Driven Development (RDD) is on by default and opt-out: run `gentle-ai review mode disable` to turn it off. Explicit global or clone-local OFF choices remain OFF. Its point is that a review cannot drift: the candidate is frozen before anything reads it, so the evidence belongs to the exact version you are about to rely on — not to whatever the worktree looked like a moment later. The depth comes from that frozen candidate rather than from the model's judgment, and the result is informational. Commit, push and release stay your call. Review is proportionate: an automatic review is due only for a high-risk candidate, and the agent can name the 4R lenses that fit what it touched — with a reason frozen alongside the authority — instead of paying for all four. Verification by risk tier covers the rest. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d3b176f-6e59-48f3-aba2-1196f20a4a6f **[Docs →](docs/review-integration.md)** --- ### Deterministic by design — Know the next valid step A model that guesses the next step guesses differently tomorrow, and differently again for your teammate. That is the gap between a workflow and a suggestion. The **`gentle-ai` binary** owns native RDD review transitions; ODD guidance keeps ordinary work proportional to the request. Review evidence is bound to the candidate rather than a model's recollection. **[Docs →](docs/trigger-rules.md)** --- ### Gentle Shell — A complete workspace for Pi Gentle Shell is a separate Pi integration package. Gentle AI configures supported agents; Gentle Shell owns its own Pi runtime, agents, and interface. Installing or updating this binary does not itself establish Pi behavior parity. On a clean machine, the [Gentle Shell installers](https://github.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-shell#get-started) set up a self-contained, bundled Gentle Shell with its exact Pi, its pinned Gentle AI, and Engram. **[Docs →](docs/pi.md)** --- ### 17 agents — Keep the agent you already use Gentle-AI brings its shared workflow to Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, and thirteen more agents. Each integration uses that agent's native capabilities, so available features such as delegation and RDD review can differ. **[Docs →](docs/agents.md)** --- ### Also in the box | Component | What it does | | :--- | :--- | | **Skills library** | Loaded automatically when the task matches | | **Context7 MCP** | Optional, selectable live framework and library documentation | | **CodeGraph** | Read-only symbol graph of your codebase | | **Security deny-list** | Blocks `~/.ssh`, `.env` and credential files | | **Config backups** | Snapshotted before every single write | | **Doctor** | `gentle-ai doctor` — read-only health report | | **Personas** | Optional personas; Gentleman is a caring but rigorous mentor who guides you toward your goal | | **Themes** | Gentleman and Gentleman-Cute | | **Model assignment** | Configure supported agent and review-role models where available | > **Every component, skill and preset: [Full breakdown →](docs/components.md)**

## Get started ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) brew install gentleman-programming/tap/gentle-ai # macOS / Linux (curl) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/main/scripts/install.sh | bash # Windows (PowerShell) — source install of the latest release, needs Go 1.25.10+ go install github.com/gentleman-programming/gentle-ai/v4/cmd/gentle-ai@v4.1.1 ``` When the install directory is not on your `PATH` yet, `install.sh` adds one marked line (`# gentle-ai installer`) to the startup file your shell reads: `~/.zshrc` for zsh, `~/.bashrc` for bash on Linux, for bash on macOS the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, or `~/.profile` (else `~/.bash_profile`), a `conf.d` file for fish, and `~/.profile` otherwise. `install.ps1` adds the directory to your user `Path`. Open a new terminal afterwards, or run the command the installer prints under `Current terminal:` to use `gentle-ai` in the current one. If the startup file is a symlink or cannot be edited, nothing is written and the installer prints the line to add yourself. `go install` never changes your `PATH`. It puts `gentle-ai` in `$(go env GOBIN)` or, when that is unset, in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` (usually `~/go/bin`), and Go's Linux and macOS setups do not add that directory for you. If `gentle-ai` is not found after `go install`, add it once and open a new terminal (use your `GOBIN` directory instead when it is set, and `~/.zshrc` for zsh): ```bash echo "export PATH=\"$(go env GOPATH)/bin:\$PATH\"" >> ~/.bashrc ``` To install `main` with the `PATH` set up for you, use `install.sh --channel beta`, which runs `go install` from `main` and then adds its directory as described above: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gentleman-Programming/gentle-ai/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel beta ``` ```bash gentle-ai # pick your agents, components and persona gentle-ai doctor # verify — read-only, changes nothing ``` If `doctor` cannot read `state.json`, inspect the reported file and parent directory's access; for permission errors, check permissions and ownership. Keep the existing state file. For invalid JSON, restore a valid backup or repair the content while preserving your installation settings. Then re-run `gentle-ai doctor`; it never changes the file or its permissions. Then use your agent normally. Your configs are snapshotted before every write, and **Gentle-AI never installs an AI agent for you** — it configures what you already have. > **Beta channel and per-distro prerequisites: [Quickstart →](docs/quickstart.md) · Signature verification: [Release signing →](docs/release-signing.md#user-verification)**
